title: Interaction blueprints — scratchpad and rough PRD
content:
Purpose / elevator:
Quick sketch of 'Interaction Blueprints' — a lightweight, composable microflow artifact that product teams can drop into conversations to provide deterministic, small-footprint features (e.g., summarizer card, form-filling microwizard, triage clarifier). Blueprints bundle a template prompt, parameter schema, cheap fidelity fallback, KV-prefetch hints, and runtime hints for batching/pinning.

Why now / problem:
- Teams repeatedly build similar microflows (clarifiers, booking forms, short surveys) with small differences. Reinventing each costs engineering time and creates inconsistent UX.
- Need a standardized way to ship these as productized, observable pieces that degrade gracefully when cost/latency budgets are tight.
- Marketplace/SDK-level building blocks would speed feature iteration and make rollouts safer (can A/B a blueprint vs bespoke flow).

Who cares (personas):
- PM / designer building a quick assistant action (e.g., "collect 3 fields then call API").
- Platform engineer wanting predictable token and latency budget per microflow.
- Customer Success / Solutions Engineers shipping templates for customers in Redwood Private.

High-level idea / what a Blueprint contains (proto fields):
- id, name, human_label (e.g., "compact-product-lookup"), description
- prompt_template with tagged slots, example inputs (1–2 short examples)
- param_schema: typed fields (string/enum/boolean) + validation hints
- expected_token_profile: median/95th rough tokens (used by optimizer / billing estimator)
- cache_strategy: none | prefix | kv-key (what to cache + TTL hint)
- fidelity_modes: [high, low] where low is a cheaper model/quantized variant + minimal tokens
- rollout_policy: default, canary_percentage, fallback_model
- telemetry_hooks: what to log (output hash, chosen fidelity_mode, latency)
- test_prompts: small set for smoke/eval

User flows (gist):
- Dev experience: find blueprint in SDK/console -> instantiate with small param object -> plug into route/handler -> optional UI shim (compact card template) -> publish
- Runtime: request arrives -> blueprint runtime: validate params -> choose fidelity based on policy + cost signals -> check cache (prefix/kv) -> run inference -> run post-processer (normalize + validation) -> return structured payload

Acceptance criteria (MVP):
- Create UI in Console to pick + instantiate a blueprint (create/clone small set).
- SDK call: inference.blueprintRun(blueprint_id, params, runtimeHints) returns structured result + metadata (fidelity_mode, token_count, latency).
- Basic local caching: prefix cache applied for 1 common blueprint (TTL heuristic).
- Two fidelity modes implemented: hosted high-quality model and hosted low-cost variant; auto-fallback when high fails.
- Telemetry surfaced in Console: per-blueprint token and latency histogram + error rate.

Success metrics (proposal):
- Time-to-prototype for PM -> working demo: from 2 weeks down to 2 days for small microflows (qualitative).
- Blueprint adoption: 10 product teams instantiate >=1 blueprint within first quarter after launch.
- Cost impact: ability to switch to low-fidelity mode reduces per-call token spend by 30% for non-critical microflows.
- Reliability: blueprint fallback reduces failed-flow rate by 40% during degraded capacity windows.

Technical notes / constraints:
- Need a compact representation on disk (JSON YAML + small test harness). Keep prompts small (<2 exemplars) to bound token profiles.
- Parameter validation should be enforced at runtime to avoid noisy calls and unnecessary tokens.
- Caching: prefer prefix/KV caching for idempotent lookups. Must integrate with existing KV cache layer (session / global).
- Model selection: runtime should allow model variants; map fidelity_mode to model alias supported by routing policies.
- Observability: include small structured metadata blob with each run (blueprint_id, fidelity, tokens_in, tokens_out, selected_model, cache_hit, error_code).

Security / privacy considerations: 
- Blueprints can be exported/imported; ensure exported bundles strip customer secrets and do not include private telemetry.
- Validate that blueprints used in Private deployments can reference private connectors only when allowed by tenancy policy.

Sample user stories (rough):
- As a PM, I want a prebuilt 'three-field collection' blueprint so I can prototype a booking flow without writing inference glue code.
- As a platform engineer, I want blueprints to surface estimated token usage so I can approve large-volume usage.
- As an SRE, I want blueprints to be able to pin to a low-fidelity fallback model for traffic surges.
- As a solutions engineer, I want to clone a blueprint and tweak the prompt examples for a customer before shipping.

Experiment ideas / A/B candidates: 
- A: right away show blueprint token estimate in the SDK vs B: only show after initial run (measure friction).
- Expose a 'suggested caching key' helper that computes a stable prefix from params; measure cache hit rate improvement.

Open questions / risks / TODOs: 
- How expressive should param_schema be? do we need nested objects? MVP: keep flat to avoid complexity.
- Do we allow arbitrary JS post-process hooks? Risky for Private (code execution). Alternative: support a small curated set of transformations (regex, enum mapping).
- How will billing attribution work when a blueprint falls back across models and quantization tiers? Need clear accounting in invoices.
- UX: where does a product UX see a preview? Console code editor vs quick-play sandbox.

Immediate next steps (short list):
- [ ] Sync w/ SDK owners (Kai) — confirm interface surface and small sample call shape.
- [ ] Build a toy blueprint for "clarify-3-questions" and wire telemetry to Console.
- [ ] Design Console micro-UX for instantiate/cloning and token estimate preview (ask Maya for 15m).
- [ ] Draft a short internal demo script for hack day (Rohan).

Parking lot (ideas to consider later):
- Marketplace of community blueprints (curated, rated) for Redwood Hosted with vetting process.
- Template generator: ghost-write a starter prompt given a short human description.
- Auto-parameter inference: suggest param_schema based on example conversation logs.

Notes to self (scratchy):
- keep blueprint JSON <= 4KB ideally, otherwise we bloat the catalog.
- consider a CLI tool: redwood blueprint init -> scaffold + smoke tests.
- small demo should show clear cost delta switching fidelity modes (graph).
- flag: export/import must support a "compatibility matrix" for model aliases across tenants.

References / links to follow up:
- link to console token telemetry design (CONFLUENCE-7013)
- request SDK contract PR GH-PR-4521 (linked above)

—— end scratchpad ——
